items.headline: Anthropic put message threads on the Messages API in beta, keeping a conversation on the server so each request sends only the new messages
items.summary: The 2 November release note says the feature, enabled with the message-threads-2026-08-12 beta header, cuts request size and time to first token for long conversations and agent loops; a thread expires 5 minutes after its last request and is deleted no more than an hour after its last use. It is available on the Claude API, the Claude Platform on AWS, Anthropic-managed Claude on Google Cloud and Claude in Microsoft Foundry.
items.why: If you run long agent loops against the Messages API, the beta stops you resending the whole transcript on every turn, but a thread dies after five idle minutes, so treat it as a latency and bandwidth win, not as persistence.

items.headline: Anthropic told the SEC it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy's threshold for AI-accelerated AI development, and raised its disclosed compute commitments to $895.4 billion
items.summary: The amended S-1 filed on 2 November says internal estimates for future models, not current ones, indicate the company may imminently meet the policy's definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI, that it does not expect to be able to safely let Claude design and build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision, and that it is considering updates to the policy to keep humans in control; it also states that over 90% of contributions to its codebase in September were written by Claude. Purchase commitments and leases, substantially all for compute and infrastructure, total about $895.4 billion, with $447.5 billion due before the end of 2030 and $69.8 billion in the next twelve months; the first filing on 26 October had described about $430 billion of cloud compute contracts. Revenue grew 1,127% year over year in the third quarter and 1,206% over the nine months.
items.why: A frontier lab has now said in a document it is legally liable for that its next models may cross its own self-improvement tripwire, so watch the promised policy rewrite and the pace of the $447.5 billion of spending due by 2030 rather than the offering price.

items.headline: GitHub delayed the default block on pull_request_target in public repositories from 2 November to 2 December and scheduled two brownouts first
items.summary: The changelog post of 2 November says Actions will block the event by default in all public repositories on GitHub Free, Team and Enterprise Cloud from 2 December unless an Actions event policy explicitly allows it, with brownouts on 9 and 16 November from 16:00 to 18:00 UTC during which affected runs fail with an error annotation; outside those windows the rule stays in evaluate mode and runs with warnings. Private, internal and Enterprise Server repositories are not affected, and policies can be targeted at specific workflow files.
items.why: If a public repository you maintain uses pull_request_target for label bots, preview deploys or fork CI with secrets, check Actions insights for would-be-blocked runs before 9 November and allowlist that workflow file or migrate, or those jobs fail for two hours on each brownout day and for good on 2 December.

items.headline: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised the cash rate to 4.85% on a 6–3 vote, its fifth increase this year and the highest rate since 2008
items.summary: The board lifted the target from 4.60%, with three members preferring to hold, and said inflation will stay above 3% for the coming year and not return to the top of the 2–3% band until late 2027, about three quarters later than previously forecast, citing oil supply disruptions feeding through to other goods and services. It noted that housing prices have fallen significantly and said it will continue to do what it considers necessary to bring inflation sustainably back to target.
items.why: Australia is the major economy tightening hardest against the oil shock, with the next decision on 8 December, so do not price Australian cuts and expect its cash rate near 5% through 2027 unless the Iran talks deliver.

items.headline: Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77 after Trump and Iranian officials signalled a negotiated end to the war
items.summary: WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46 on 2 November, its biggest daily loss since 27 July, after Trump said Iran wants to make a deal, Rubio said the US would prefer to resolve the conflict peacefully and had not decided on further strikes, and Foreign Minister Araghchi said an agreement is possible if Washington demonstrates goodwill, with Tehran asking for sanctions relief and an end to the blockade. Oil had risen more than 10% in October on the risk of escalation after the US midterms.
items.why: The energy inflation that drove today's RBA hike and the ECB's and BoJ's hawkish turn can unwind in a day if the talks hold, so do not extrapolate October's oil price into rate forecasts.

items.headline: The People's Bank of China made the overnight reverse repo rate, 1.25%, its main policy rate, replacing the seven-day rate
items.summary: From 2 November the central bank conducts overnight reverse repos every working day at a fixed 1.25% through quantity bidding, and its first operation under the new mechanism injected 541 billion yuan (about $80.6 billion); tools previously priced off the seven-day rate, such as temporary repos, are now linked to the overnight rate with their spreads unchanged. Governor Pan Gongsheng had said in October the shift would improve the precision of interest rate regulation.
items.why: China's policy rate is now the 1.25% overnight rate, so read PBoC easing or tightening from that number from here on and expect the seven-day rate to fade from the headlines.

items.headline: Binance saw $3.64 billion of net outflows in the first nine and a half hours after reopening withdrawals, 2.1% of its assets, and said its zero-knowledge proof of reserves would follow a ten-asset snapshot
items.summary: Binance processed $4.65 billion of withdrawals against $1.01 billion of deposits between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC on 1 November, and DeFiLlama's 24-hour net outflow later eased to about $3.29 billion; the exchange said it had replaced about 95% of the stolen assets, that the remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still acquiring, and that it would restore further networks from 3 November. Its new proof-of-reserves snapshot covers BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC, with co-CEO Yi He saying the proof takes 40 to 50 hours after the snapshot and a further snapshot with more tokens planned for 4 November; Circle has frozen more than $1.1 billion of USDC linked to the theft.
items.why: Users are pulling about 2% of Binance's assets a day while the full proof is still unpublished, so if you are moving funds out, use a network that has already reopened rather than waiting for yours.
